title: The Rogue Council
summary: An unseen group that signs its messages with a sphinx.

claims.text: Since the Reckoning, many mages call cowardice prudence and see waking the masses as a fool's hope; the Rogue Council's messages call them back to action.
It argues for liberty over dogma and choice over Technocratic stasis, and it attacks autocratic Traditionalists as well as the Union.
The Council itself does very little in the open; its readers do the acting, and its messages stir debate and inspire deeds.

title: Sphinx missives
summary: How the Rogue Council reaches mages.

claims.text: A missive may arrive as an unsigned letter bearing a sphinx, with no arcane trail to its author, paper or carriers even under divination.
Its creed runs on themes such as unity through diversity, Ascension through freedom, and exploring the path rather than building it.
The same message often reaches many mages at once, from wandering scholars to young Virtual Adepts online.

title: Answers to the Sphinx
summary: How mages react to the Rogue Council.

claims.text: Most mages act on a missive carefully, checking first and often consulting their elders; some are only waiting to see which way events turn.
No one knows if ignoring a missive brings punishment, though some who ignored them have died.
Many Tradition mages call the creed a reckless youthful call to anarchy, and some sages hold that outward struggle is mistaken for inner growth.
Those most devoted to the new creed are mostly too young to know how harsh a Technocratic pogrom can be.

title: Emissaries and Guardians
summary: The split the Rogue Council opened.

claims.text: Mages who back the Rogue Council are called Emissaries and those against it Guardians; neither side is wholly right.
About six months into the phenomenon, messages began naming cabals that had won victories against the Technocracy, along with field reports on Union methods.
Quarrels over the Council's supposed creed grew into open enmity, and certamen between Emissaries and Guardians was common for a while.

title: The Union and the transmissions
summary: How Technocrats meet Rogue Council messages.

claims.text: The Technocracy tries to suppress the messages, and some Constructs order collectors of them caught or killed.
Most front-line agents dismiss the transmissions as Deviant chatter, but a few cannot answer the questions they raise about Union projects.
Secret societies inside the Union, such as the Friends of Courage and the Harbingers of Avalon, have long resisted Control's orders on moral grounds.
